column1: # labels_recall.tsv — held-out labels for the RECALL lane (the retrieval-evaluation plan
# the measuring instrument that must exist before the generated-doc demotion — default de-prioritization of generated docs in
# the recall lens — may be evaluated). One row per query: query<TAB>primary<TAB>acceptable<TAB>class
#   primary    = comma-separated repo-relative markdown path(s); a hit on ANY of them is primary credit.
#   acceptable = comma-separated path(s) earning lenient (graded) credit, or `-` for none.
#   class      = name | concept | task | adversarial
#                name        — the query names the doc or its title nearly verbatim
#                concept     — conceptual phrase answered by exactly one design/research doc
#                task        — an agent's task-shaped question whose answer is a doc
#                adversarial — a query whose TOP LEXICAL match is expected to be a generated capture
#                              (docs/captures/COMMANDS_showcase_*.md quotes every verb and flag), while
#                              the labelled right answer is the real hand-written doc.
# LABELING PROTOCOL (held-out means held out): every label below was authored by READING the candidate
# documents' actual content (titles + bodies) and deciding which doc ANSWERS the query — never by running
# `--recall` and transcribing what the current ranker returns. The ranker was run on these queries only
# AFTER this file was complete, to produce baseline numbers. The eval is therefore allowed to say the
# current ranker is wrong.
# Corpus note: the recall lens is docs-only (markdown). These labels were authored against the private
# development tree's document set, much of which this public export deliberately does not ship. The
# harness counts a query whose labelled paths are absent on disk as SKIPPED (reported), so the checkout
# degrades honestly rather than scoring a query it cannot answer -- but the RECALL LANE IS THEREFORE
# UNDER-SAMPLED HERE AND MUST BE RE-AUTHORED against this repo's own docs/ set before its numbers mean
# anything. Re-author by READING the shipped docs, never by transcribing --recall output (see the
# labeling protocol above). The ranking lane, which targets code, is unaffected.
